"''Get Admiral Gorin, immediately!|Casido orders Gorin to be brought to the bridge|audio=Casido.flac|}} '''Casido''' was a [[human]] [[lieutenant]] in the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[1 BBY]], they were stationed on the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Intimidator]]'' and witnessed the arrival of a [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Rebel Alliance fleet]] above the [[planet]] [[Scarif]] from its [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]]. Casido called for someone to get [[Admiral]] [[Gorin]], but after the admiral arrived on the bridge the ''Intimidator'' was destroyed in the ensuing conflict. ==Biography== Casido was a [[human]] [[Imperial Navy's officer corps|officer]] in the [[Imperial Navy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' to [[1 BBY]]. they held the [[Military rank|rank]] of [[lieutenant]] and were stationed on board the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]]''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' ''[[Intimidator]]''''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' while it was part of the [[Scarif fleet|fleet]] that defended the [[Imperial Center of Military Research]] on the [[planet]] [[Scarif]]. When a [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Rebel Alliance fleet]] jumped into the [[Scarif system]] in order to support a [[Rogue One|group]] of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebels]] who had slipped passed the Imperials and made it to Scarif's surface to [[Battle of Scarif|steal]] the [[Death Star plans|plans]] to the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]], Casido was stood on the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] of the ''Intimidator''. [[File:Intimidator-PersecutorCrash.png|thumb|left|300px|Casido served on the ''Intimidator'' (bottom) which was destroyed at the Battle of Scarif.]] Witnessing the arrival of the [[fleet]] through the [[viewport]], the lieutenant shouted orders for someone to fetch [[Admiral]] [[Gorin]], [[Orbital Command]] of the Scarif fleet.''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' Gorin then arrived on the bridge at some point during the ensuing conflict between the rebels and Imperials, which culminated in the destruction of the ''Intimidator'' when the disabled [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Persecutor]]'' was forced to collide with it, allowing the rebels to successfully steal the plans. ==Personality and traits== Casido had light skin, [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s, and brown [[hair]]. ==Equipment== Casido wore the [[Imperial military uniforms|uniform]] of an [[Imperial officer]], including an [[Imperial kepi]] with an [[officer's disk]] and another disk on the buckle of their [[belt]]. The [[officer]] had a [[code cylinder]] on each [[breast]] and a [[rank insignia plaque]] with three blue pips and two red. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|X-wings are dropping!|Rufus Wright delivering one of Casido's cut lines of dialogue|audio=Wright-XWings.flac|{{YouTube|video=T6vqyqwCiyE|text=Star Wars Rufus Wright Interview Rogue One Lt. Casido|channel=@RedCarpetNewsTV|name=Red Carpet News TV|date=2017-06-11}}}} [[File:RufusWright-BBC.png|thumb|right|280px|Casido was portrayed by Rufus Wright.]] Casido was portrayed by [[Rufus Wright]] in the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|Anthology Series]] film, ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. The character's name is not spoken in the film but Wright's character is named as Lieutenant Casido in the credits. Wright filmed a large amount of dialogue as Casido, including lines about [[X-wing starfighter]]s, but most of it was cut from the film's final release. The scenes involved Gorin's actor, [[Michael Gould]], and also included lines about the ''Intimidator'' being under repair and so unable to move. The scenes were blocked out by director [[Gareth Edwards]] before being filmed on a gimble on a sound stage set by the film's second unit.{{WebCite|url=https://www.spyhards.com/e/spymaster-interview-36-rufus-wright|text=SpyMaster Interview #36 - Rufus Wright|date=2022-12-08|format=[[Wikipedia:Podcast|Podcast]]|work=[https://www.spyhards.com SpyHards - A Spy Movie Podcast]|archivedate=20230131094645}} A chart of Imperial rank insignia created for ''Rogue One'' and released by costume designer [[Glyn Dillon]]{{Instagram|username=glyn__dillon|url=p/BcDdpV7BNP1|name=[[Glyn Dillon]]|date=2017-11-28|quote=I sometimes get asked, on Twitter, about certain things to do with the details of Star Wars costumes, especially Imperial costumes. I try to answer as best I can but I can't always remember… 'ranking' is something that crops up every now and then …so I've been meaning to post this on here for a while. My co-designer, David Crossman is a military expert, much like John Mollo was, so this is something he put together, after studying all the OT films and working out what he thought John Mollo was doing with the Imperial ranking. It was devised for Rogue One… and if there are any Imperials in Solo, we would've have used this system again… But obviously I can't say if we did 😜 I hope it's useful for all the cosplayers and costumers out there|archivefile=File:Imperial_Forces_Rank_Chart_-_Rogue_One.png}} lists the plaque worn by Casido as being that of a [[Navy|naval]] [[captain]] rather than a lieutenant. ==Appearances== {{Indexpage}} *''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1st}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |fr=Casido |ja=キャシド }} [[Category:Humans]] [[Category:Imperial Navy officers of the Galactic Empire]] [[Category:Individuals of unspecified gender]] [[Category:Individuals with unspecified pronouns]]
